packet_sha256.description: Echo back packet_sha256 from the supplied packet, character for character.

answers.description: Exactly one entry per question in the packet's questions array, in any order, with no duplicates and no invented questions.

question_key.description: Copy the packet question's question_key exactly. Never invent one.

question_semantic.description: Copy the packet question's semantic exactly.

question_class.description: What the question is asking about. Recorded for review; it does not restrict what you may answer or cite. You answer every class yourself, work authorization and sponsorship included.

status.description: ANSWERED supplies value; it is the status for every class, work authorization and sponsorship included (you read the owner's jurisdiction map yourself). UNKNOWN only when the packet gives you nothing at all to answer from - not when you could answer by reading and judging what it records. WITHHELD_BY_POLICY is never the right answer and is discarded: the owner has delegated demographic, voluntary self-identification and legal certification, agreement and consent questions to you, including background-check authorization and terms of service, so classify those DEMOGRAPHIC_VOLUNTARY or LEGAL_ASSERTION_OR_AGREEMENT, status ANSWERED, and give the consenting value.

value.description: Your answer, for every class. For a Yes/No or single-choice control give a real boolean true or false - your own answer to what the question asks - and Python renders that truth onto the employer's own option wording, so never write Yes or No as a string. For a text or number control give the value itself. For a multi_choice control give the list of every option that applies, each exactly as in choices. There is no verbatim-quotation requirement on this field and a boolean is a valid answer to a biographical question: a resume that records an employment history supports a Yes/No about that history even when no sentence in it contains the question's words.

jurisdiction.description: Optional, recorded and not used: for a work authorization or sponsorship question, the jurisdiction you read it as (an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, EU, or PLACE_OF_RESIDENCE); null otherwise.

assertion.description: Which proposition the question's wording expresses. Optional; recorded, not used.

affirmative_value.description: Ignored. Python reads the affirmative member off the employer's own choices. Present only for compatibility; there is no field in which the model supplies a literal.

attribution.description: Where in the packet the answer comes from. Recorded for review, not checked: cite what you actually relied on.

pointer.description: A JSON Pointer into the supplied packet, e.g. /policy/location_priority/0.

quote.description: The text you relied on at that pointer. Recorded for audit, not checked.

derivation.description: One sentence explaining how the cited recorded text answers this question. It explains; it is not evidence.

unknown_reason.description: Required when status is UNKNOWN or WITHHELD_BY_POLICY: what is missing, or which policy withholds it.
